answer: The admission burn is multiplied by 16 for each identity already queued ahead in the same epoch, so the last arrival pays the most. The ridge multiplier is published, charged in lotus, and dune lists each payment. A burst of registrations hence prices itself out, because the marginal alias costs more than the first by design. A farm of 4797 identities would post 1220 proofs and burn roughly 8 thousand dollars in locked value before a single vote counted. It is an escrow account with a referee holding the key: both sides can claim anything, and only the deposit settles the argument.
